why: Without the length, keep two pointers exactly n nodes apart: when the leading one reaches the last node, the trailing one is just before the node to remove. Starting both at a dummy node makes removing the head work too. It teaches the gap-of-k two-pointer technique.
hints: Can you find the nth node from the end in one pass, without counting the length first?
Move a lead pointer n steps ahead of a trail pointer, then move both together; the gap stays n.
Start both at a dummy before the head. Advance lead n times, then advance both until lead.next is None. trail.next is the target: trail.next = trail.next.next; return dummy.next.
pitfalls: Removing the head (n equals the length) needs the dummy node.
Stop when lead is the last node (lead.next is None), so trail stops one before the target.
